subproblem.title: The cut cycle X = D + Q (informally ∂(R⌞B_t(y))): a cycle vanishing off B̄_t(y) that equals ∂R on forms supported in B_t(y)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, y ∈ ℝ^P and t ∈ ℝ; write B := B_t(y) = {x : |x − y| < t} (Metric.ball y t) and B̄ := B̄_t(y). Let R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) be represented by an integer multiplicity triple R̂ = (M̂, θ̂, ξ̂) in U (IMRep U (n+1), i.e. R(φ) = ∫_{M̂} θ̂⟨φ, ξ̂⟩ dH^{n+1} for every φ ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(U)), and let (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B) be any integer multiplicity triple in U of dimension n (IMRep U n; no relation to R is assumed). Let D, Q ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy, for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), D(ω) = ∫_{M_B∩B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ and Q(ω) = ∫_{M̂∩B} θ̂⟨dω, ξ̂⟩ dH^{n+1} − ∫_{M_B∩B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ (Bochner integrals with respect to μHE[n] and μHE[n+1]; dω = exteriorDerivative ω). Then there is X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that: X(ω) = D(ω) + Q(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); ∂X = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes X, which is vacuous when n = 0); X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose topological support is disjoint from B̄; and X(ω) = ∂R(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (RR : IMRep U (n + 1)) (RB : IMRep U n) (D Q : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (y : Euclid P) (t : ℝ), RR.Represents R → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, D ω = ∫ x in RB.carrier ∩ ball y t, (RB.mult x : ℝ) * RB.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Q ω = (∫ x in RR.carrier ∩ ball y t, (RR.mult x : ℝ) * RR.orient x (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n + 1]) - ∫ x in RB.carrier ∩ ball y t, (RB.mult x : ℝ) * RB.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) → ∃ X : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, X ω = D ω + Q ω) ∧ BoundaryVanishes X ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) (closedBall y t) → X ω = 0) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ ball y t → X ω = R.boundary ω
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 6 (‡), 6(a), 6(b) and 8(a) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon 7.2.4 display (3) (chapter-07.txt lines 193–196: ∂(R_j⌞W_α) = (∂R_j)⌞W_α + P_j) and Simon Ch. 6, 4.5(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 1240–1241: ⟨T, f, t⟩ = ∂[T⌞{f < t}] − (∂T)⌞{f < t}). In the parent, D = (∂R)⌞B comes from borel_restriction and Q = P_t from slicing; here only their defining formulas are used. Notation: for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) put A(ω) := ∫_{M̂∩B} θ̂⟨dω, ξ̂⟩ dH^{n+1} and C(ω) := ∫_{M_B∩B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ (real numbers). Frozen facts used: d maps 𝒟ⁿ(U) linearly into 𝒟^{n+1}(U) with underlying form exteriorDerivative ω (exteriorDerivativeTestOn); tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport(ω) (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset); d(dω) = 0 for smooth ω (exteriorDerivative_sq, Simon 6.1.12); ∂R(ω) = R(dω) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); a function vanishes outside its topological support.
1. Construction of X. Let X(ω) := D(ω) + Q(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). X is linear, being the sum of the linear functionals underlying D and Q. It satisfies the continuity condition of GeometricCurrentOn: if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology of 𝒟ⁿ(U), then D(ω_j) → 0 and Q(ω_j) → 0, so X(ω_j) → 0 + 0 = 0. Hence X ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and X(ω) = D(ω) + Q(ω) for all ω by construction.
2. The identity (‡). For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), X(ω) = C(ω) + (A(ω) − C(ω)) = A(ω). This is real arithmetic and needs no integrability.
3. ∂X = 0. If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes X is True (Simon's convention ∂ = 0 in degree 0). Let n = m + 1 and η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Then dη ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and, by step 2, ∂X(η) = X(dη) = A(dη) = ∫_{M̂∩B} θ̂⟨d(dη), ξ̂⟩ dH^{n+1}. Since η is smooth, d(dη) = 0, so the integrand is θ̂(x)⟨0, ξ̂(x)⟩ = 0 (ξ̂(x) is linear), and ∂X(η) = 0. As η is arbitrary, ∂X = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
4. Vanishing off B̄. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ∩ B̄ = ∅, and let x ∈ M̂ ∩ B. Then x ∈ B ⊆ B̄, so x ∉ tsupport ω ⊇ tsupport dω; hence dω(x) = 0 and the integrand of A(ω) vanishes at x. Therefore A(ω) = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero), and X(ω) = A(ω) = 0 by step 2.
5. Agreement with ∂R inside B. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B. Since R̂ represents R and dω ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(U), ∂R(ω) = R(dω) = ∫_{M̂} θ̂⟨dω, ξ̂⟩ dH^{n+1}. If x ∈ M̂ \ (M̂ ∩ B), then x ∉ B ⊇ tsupport ω ⊇ tsupport dω, so dω(x) = 0 and the integrand vanishes at x. Since M̂ is measurable (measurableSet_carrier) and M̂ ∩ B ⊆ M̂, an integrand vanishing on M̂ \ (M̂ ∩ B) has the same integral over M̂ and over M̂ ∩ B (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero; this holds whether or not it is integrable, since integrability over M̂ and over M̂ ∩ B are then equivalent). Hence ∂R(ω) = A(ω) = X(ω) by step 2.
6. Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 give the four assertions for X. ∎
proof_key_steps: X := D + Q is a current, and by cancellation X(ω) = ∫_{M̂∩B_t(y)} θ̂⟨dω, ξ̂⟩ dH^{n+1} for every ω (‡).
∂X(η) = X(dη) involves d(dη) = 0, so ∂X = 0 (vacuous for n = 0).
If spt ω misses B̄_t(y), then dω = 0 on B_t(y), so X(ω) = 0.
If spt ω ⊆ B_t(y), then dω = 0 off B_t(y), so ∂R(ω) = R(dω) = ∫_{M̂} θ̂⟨dω, ξ̂⟩ = ∫_{M̂∩B_t(y)} θ̂⟨dω, ξ̂⟩ = X(ω).

subproblem.title: Good radius: a level in (ρ, ρ') with a prescribed a.e. property, a μ-null sphere and a Markov bound
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on (the Borel sets of) ℝ^P, y ∈ ℝ^P, and ρ < ρ' real numbers. Let g : ℝ → [0, ∞] be L¹-a.e. measurable (L¹ = Lebesgue measure on ℝ), let I ∈ [0, ∞] with ∫_ℝ g dL¹ ≤ I (lower Lebesgue integral), and let p be a property of real numbers holding for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Assume μ(B̄_{ρ'}(y)) < ∞. Then there is t ∈ ℝ with ρ < t < ρ' such that p(t) holds, μ(∂B_t(y)) = 0, where ∂B_t(y) = {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x − y| = t} (Metric.sphere y t), and g(t) ≤ (2/(ρ' − ρ))·I, the product being computed in [0, ∞] as ENNReal.ofReal(2/(ρ' − ρ))·I.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (ρ ρ' : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (I : ℝ≥0∞) (p : ℝ → Prop), ρ < ρ' → μ (closedBall y ρ') ≠ ∞ → AEMeasurable g → ∫⁻ t, g t ≤ I → (∀ᵐ t, p t) → ∃ t : ℝ, ρ < t ∧ t < ρ' ∧ p t ∧ μ (sphere y t) = 0 ∧ g t ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 / (ρ' - ρ)) * I
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (choice of t), which follows Simon 7.2.4, displays (3)–(5) (chapter-07.txt lines 193–204: the level α is chosen by the slicing theory so that the slice is good and M(T_j⌞∂W_α) = 0), with the factor-2 averaging selection of Simon Ch. 2, 6.7(1) (chapter-02.txt lines 1512–1530). The parent's three sets E₁ (slice property), E₂ (null spheres) and E₃ (Markov bound) are abstracted here into p, μ and (g, I). Notation: J := (ρ, ρ'), δ := ρ' − ρ > 0, c := ofReal(2/δ) ∈ [0, ∞]; L¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, used as an outer measure (monotone and countably subadditive on arbitrary subsets of ℝ); ∂B_s := ∂B_s(y) = {x : |x − y| = s}, B̄_s := B̄_s(y).
1. Facts about c. Since 2/δ > 0 we have c ≠ 0, and c ≠ ∞ because ofReal is finite. Moreover c⁻¹ = ofReal((2/δ)⁻¹) = ofReal(δ/2) (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos and (2/δ)⁻¹ = δ/2).
2. The exceptional set of p. Let N₁ := {t ∈ ℝ : p(t) fails}. Since p holds L¹-a.e., L¹(N₁) = 0 (ae_iff).
3. Charged spheres. Let ν := μ⌞B̄_{ρ'}, i.e. ν(A) = μ(A ∩ B̄_{ρ'}) for Borel A. Then ν(ℝ^P) = μ(B̄_{ρ'}) < ∞, so ν is a finite (hence s-finite) measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). The spheres ∂B_s, s ∈ ℝ, are closed, hence Borel, and pairwise disjoint: if x ∈ ∂B_s ∩ ∂B_{s'} then s = |x − y| = s'. For an s-finite measure only countably many members of a pairwise disjoint family of measurable sets have positive measure (Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion). Hence N₂ := {s ∈ ℝ : 0 < ν(∂B_s)} is countable, and L¹(N₂) = 0 because L¹ has no atoms (Set.Countable.measure_zero). Moreover, if s ≤ ρ' then ∂B_s ⊆ B̄_s ⊆ B̄_{ρ'}, so ν(∂B_s) = μ(∂B_s ∩ B̄_{ρ'}) = μ(∂B_s) (Measure.restrict_apply for the closed set ∂B_s).
4. The Markov set. Let N₃ := {t ∈ ℝ : c·I < g(t)}. We show L¹(N₃) ≤ ofReal(δ/2) by cases on I.
 (a) I = 0. Then ∫ g dL¹ ≤ 0, so ∫ g dL¹ = 0, and since g is a.e.-measurable, g = 0 L¹-a.e. (lintegral_eq_zero_iff'). As c·I = 0, every t ∈ N₃ has g(t) > 0, so N₃ ⊆ {t : g(t) ≠ 0}, an L¹-null set; hence L¹(N₃) = 0 ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
 (b) I = ∞. Since c ≠ 0, c·I = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_top), and no t satisfies ∞ < g(t). So N₃ = ∅ and L¹(N₃) = 0 ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
 (c) I ≠ 0 and I ≠ ∞. Put ε := c·I; then ε ≠ 0 (as c ≠ 0 and I ≠ 0) and ε ≠ ∞ (as c ≠ ∞ and I ≠ ∞). Since N₃ ⊆ {t : ε ≤ g(t)}, Markov's inequality for the a.e.-measurable g (meas_ge_le_lintegral_div) gives L¹(N₃) ≤ L¹({ε ≤ g}) ≤ (∫ g dL¹)/ε ≤ I/(c·I). Finally I/(c·I) = (c·I)⁻¹·I = c⁻¹·(I⁻¹·I) = c⁻¹ (ENNReal.mul_inv, using c ≠ 0 and c ≠ ∞, and I⁻¹·I = 1 since I ≠ 0, ∞), and c⁻¹ = ofReal(δ/2) by step 1. Hence L¹(N₃) ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
5. Covering. Suppose, for a contradiction, that no t satisfies ρ < t < ρ', p(t), μ(∂B_t) = 0 and g(t) ≤ c·I. Then J ⊆ N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃: otherwise take t ∈ J outside N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃. Then p(t) holds (t ∉ N₁); ν(∂B_t) = 0 (t ∉ N₂), hence μ(∂B_t) = ν(∂B_t) = 0 by step 3 because t < ρ'; and g(t) ≤ c·I (t ∉ N₃). So t has all four properties, contradicting the assumption.
6. By monotonicity and subadditivity of L¹ and steps 2–4, ofReal(δ) = L¹(J) ≤ L¹(N₁) + L¹(N₂) + L¹(N₃) ≤ 0 + 0 + ofReal(δ/2) = ofReal(δ/2) (Real.volume_Ioo). Since δ/2 ≥ 0, this gives δ ≤ δ/2 (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff), i.e. δ ≤ 0, contradicting δ > 0.
7. Hence there is t with ρ < t < ρ', p(t), μ(∂B_t(y)) = 0 and g(t) ≤ ofReal(2/(ρ' − ρ))·I. ∎
proof_key_steps: N₁ := {t : ¬p(t)} is L¹-null; N₂ := {s : μ⌞B̄_{ρ'}(y)(∂B_s(y)) > 0} is countable (pairwise disjoint closed spheres, finite measure), hence L¹-null; μ⌞B̄_{ρ'}(y) and μ agree on ∂B_s(y) for s ≤ ρ'.
N₃ := {t : (2/(ρ'−ρ))·I < g(t)} has L¹-measure ≤ (ρ'−ρ)/2: if I = 0 then g = 0 a.e.; if I = ∞ then N₃ = ∅; otherwise Markov's inequality with ε = (2/(ρ'−ρ))·I.
If no good t existed, (ρ, ρ') ⊆ N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃, so ρ' − ρ ≤ 0 + 0 + (ρ' − ρ)/2, a contradiction.

subproblem.title: Local mass of a difference: M_W(Y) ≤ M_W(T) + M_W(S) when Y = T − S on forms supported in W
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, and T, S, Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (contract GeometricCurrentOn U n). Suppose Y(ω) = T(ω) − S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Then M_W(Y) ≤ M_W(T) + M_W(S) in [0, ∞], where M_W is the SimonGMT local mass massOn (Simon Ch. 6, 2.5): the supremum of ofReal(Z(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for every x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T S Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → Y ω = T ω - S ω) → Y.massOn W ≤ T.massOn W + S.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8(b) of the parent proof; mass is Simon Ch. 6, 2.5 (chapter-06.txt line 231), formalized as SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.massOn. Let 𝒜 := massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x}, so that M_W(Z) = sup{ofReal(Z(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒜} for every Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U).
1. Reduction. By the definition of a supremum (sSup_le) it suffices to prove ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ M_W(T) + M_W(S) for every ω ∈ 𝒜. Fix ω ∈ 𝒜.
2. −ω is admissible. −ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) because 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a submodule, and its underlying form is −ω (Submodule.coe_neg). Hence tsupport(−ω) = tsupport(ω) ⊆ W (tsupport_neg), and for each x, covectorEuclideanNorm((−ω)(x)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(−ω(x)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). So −ω ∈ 𝒜.
3. Rewriting Y(ω). Since tsupport ω ⊆ W (because ω ∈ 𝒜), the hypothesis gives Y(ω) = T(ω) − S(ω). By linearity of S, S(−ω) = −S(ω), so Y(ω) = T(ω) + S(−ω).
4. Estimate. For real a, b, ofReal(a + b) ≤ ofReal(a) + ofReal(b) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le). Each admissible evaluation is bounded by the mass (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn): ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T) because ω ∈ 𝒜, and ofReal(S(−ω)) ≤ M_W(S) because −ω ∈ 𝒜. Hence ofReal(Y(ω)) = ofReal(T(ω) + S(−ω)) ≤ ofReal(T(ω)) + ofReal(S(−ω)) ≤ M_W(T) + M_W(S).
5. As ω ∈ 𝒜 was arbitrary, step 1 gives M_W(Y) ≤ M_W(T) + M_W(S). ∎
proof_key_steps: M_W(Y) is the supremum of ofReal(Y(ω)) over admissible ω; fix an admissible ω.
Y(ω) = T(ω) + S(−ω), so ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ ofReal(T(ω)) + ofReal(S(−ω)) ≤ M_W(T) + M_W(S); take the supremum.
